it('uses the stock writer to commit central and tenant audit before login with optional audit disabled and async queue', function (): void {
    config(['corex.audit.enabled' => false, 'queue.default' => 'database']);
    $account = initAccountWithTenantIM();
    seedTenantUserIM($account, $account->owner_identity_id);
    $staffId = makeStaffIdentityIM();
    $grantId = makeGrantIM($staffId, $account->id);

    expect(app(ImpersonationService::class))->toBeInstanceOf(ImpersonationService::class)
        ->and(app(ImpersonationAuditSink::class))->toBeInstanceOf(DualImpersonationAuditSink::class)
        ->and(app(SynchronousAuditWriter::class))->toBeInstanceOf(SynchronousAuditWriter::class);
    expect(app(AuditLogger::class))->toBeInstanceOf(AuditLogger::class);
    app(ImpersonationService::class)->start($grantId, $staffId);

    $central = DB::connection('pgsql')->table('root_account_events')->where('event', 'impersonation.started')->sole();
    $tenant = DB::connection('tenant')->table('sys_audit_log')->where('action', 'impersonation.started')->sole();
    $payload = json_decode((string) $central->payload, true, 512, JSON_THROW_ON_ERROR);
    $context = json_decode((string) $tenant->context, true, 512, JSON_THROW_ON_ERROR);
    expect($payload['profile'])->toBe('standard')
        ->and($payload['expires_at'])->not->toBeNull()
        ->and($context['grant_id'])->toBe($grantId)
        ->and($tenant->actor_id)->toBe($staffId)
        ->and(Auth::guard('web')->check())->toBeTrue();

    app(ImpersonationService::class)->stop();
    expect(DB::connection('pgsql')->table('root_account_events')->where('event', 'impersonation.ended')->count())->toBe(1)
        ->and(DB::connection('tenant')->table('sys_audit_log')->where('action', 'impersonation.ended')->count())->toBe(1);
});

it('keeps committed central intent and a consumed grant when the tenant writer fails before login', function (): void {
    $account = initAccountWithTenantIM();
    seedTenantUserIM($account, $account->owner_identity_id);
    $staffId = makeStaffIdentityIM();
    $grantId = makeGrantIM($staffId, $account->id);
    app()->forgetScopedInstances();
    app()->instance(SynchronousAuditWriter::class, new class implements SynchronousAuditWriter
    {
        public function record(AuditEntry $entry, string $connectionName): void
        {
            throw new RuntimeException('tenant mirror failed');
        }
    });
    expect(fn () => app(ImpersonationService::class)->start($grantId, $staffId))->toThrow(RuntimeException::class);
    expect(grantRowIM($grantId)->used_at)->not->toBeNull()
        ->and(DB::connection('pgsql')->table('root_account_events')->where('event', 'impersonation.started')->count())->toBe(1)
        ->and(Auth::guard('web')->check())->toBeFalse()
        ->and(session('corex.impersonation.grant_id'))->toBeNull();
});

it('refuses login and consumes the grant when the central audit insert fails', function (): void {
    $account = initAccountWithTenantIM();
    seedTenantUserIM($account, $account->owner_identity_id);
    $staffId = makeStaffIdentityIM();
    $grantId = makeGrantIM($staffId, $account->id);
    DB::connection('pgsql')->statement('DROP TABLE root_account_events');

    expect(fn () => app(ImpersonationService::class)->start($grantId, $staffId))->toThrow(QueryException::class);
    expect(grantRowIM($grantId)->used_at)->not->toBeNull()
        ->and(DB::connection('tenant')->table('sys_audit_log')->count())->toBe(0)
        ->and(Auth::guard('web')->check())->toBeFalse();
});

it('rejects an ambient tenant transaction after consuming the grant', function (): void {
    $account = initAccountWithTenantIM();
    seedTenantUserIM($account, $account->owner_identity_id);
    $staffId = makeStaffIdentityIM();
    $grantId = makeGrantIM($staffId, $account->id);
    $tenant = DB::connection('tenant');
    $tenant->beginTransaction();

    try {
        expect(fn () => app(ImpersonationService::class)->start($grantId, $staffId))->toThrow(RuntimeException::class);
        expect(grantRowIM($grantId)->used_at)->not->toBeNull()
            ->and(DB::connection('pgsql')->table('root_account_events')->where('event', 'impersonation.started')->count())->toBe(0)
            ->and(Auth::guard('web')->check())->toBeFalse();
    } finally {
        $tenant->rollBack();
    }
});

it('omits tenant mirror in dev and requires production acknowledgement', function (): void {
    config(['corex-tenancy.impersonation.profile' => 'dev']);
    app()->forgetInstance(TenancyOptions::class);
    app()->forgetInstance(ImpersonationPolicy::class);
    app()->forgetScopedInstances();
    $account = initAccountWithTenantIM();
    seedTenantUserIM($account, $account->owner_identity_id);
    $staffId = makeStaffIdentityIM();
    $grantId = makeGrantIM($staffId, $account->id, ['expires_at' => now()->addHours(4)]);
    app(ImpersonationService::class)->start($grantId, $staffId);

    expect(DB::connection('pgsql')->table('root_account_events')->where('event', 'impersonation.started')->count())->toBe(1)
        ->and(DB::connection('tenant')->table('sys_audit_log')->count())->toBe(0);

    $options = app(TenancyOptions::class);
    $path = 'corex-tenancy.impersonation.profile';
    expect((new DangerousModesCheck($options, CoreOptionsParser::fromArray([])))->violations(true))->toContain($path.': dangerous mode is not acknowledged for production')
        ->and((new DangerousModesCheck($options, CoreOptionsParser::fromArray(['acknowledged_dangerous_modes' => [$path]])))->violations(true))->toBe([]);
});

declare(strict_types=1);

use CoreX\Tenancy\Impersonation\Data\GrantClaim;
use CoreX\Tenancy\Impersonation\Enums\ImpersonationProfile;
use CoreX\Tenancy\Impersonation\Internal\DatabaseImpersonationGrantStore;
use CoreX\Tenancy\Tests\TestCase;
use Illuminate\Database\ConnectionResolverInterface;
use Illuminate\Support\Facades\DB;
use Illuminate\Support\Str;

uses(TestCase::class);

it('enforces all 27 grant profile matrix cells in the atomic claim', function (): void {
    DB::statement('DROP SCHEMA IF EXISTS public CASCADE');
    DB::statement('CREATE SCHEMA public');
    DB::purge('pgsql');
    test()->artisan('migrate', [
        '--database' => 'pgsql',
        '--path' => realpath(__DIR__.'/../../database/migrations/root'),
        '--realpath' => true,
        '--force' => true,
    ])->run();

    $central = DB::connection('pgsql');
    $staffId = (string) Str::uuid();
    $approverId = (string) Str::uuid();
    $nonStaffId = (string) Str::uuid();
    $ownerId = (string) Str::uuid();
    foreach ([$staffId => true, $approverId => true, $nonStaffId => false, $ownerId => false] as $id => $staff) {
        $central->table('root_identities')->insert(['id' => $id, 'email' => $id.'@test.invalid', 'is_staff' => $staff]);
    }

    $clusterId = (string) Str::uuid();
    $accountId = (string) Str::uuid();
    $central->table('root_clusters')->insert([
        'id' => $clusterId, 'name' => 'profile-test', 'pg_host_writer' => 'localhost',
        'pgbouncer_host' => 'localhost', 'app_db_user' => 'corex',
    ]);
    $central->table('root_accounts')->insert([
        'id' => $accountId, 'cluster_id' => $clusterId, 'db_name' => 'profile_test',
        'status' => 'active', 'slug' => 'profile-test', 'owner_identity_id' => $ownerId,
        'template_version' => 1, 'embedding_model' => 'bge-m3', 'embedding_dim' => 1024,
    ]);

    $cases = [
        ['minutes' => 45, 'approver' => null, 'staff' => true, 'reason' => 'ticket', 'accepted' => [true, true, false]],
        ['minutes' => 45, 'approver' => $approverId, 'staff' => true, 'reason' => 'ticket', 'accepted' => [true, true, false]],
        ['minutes' => 20, 'approver' => $approverId, 'staff' => true, 'reason' => 'ticket', 'accepted' => [true, true, true]],
        ['minutes' => 20, 'approver' => $staffId, 'staff' => true, 'reason' => 'ticket', 'accepted' => [true, true, false]],
        ['minutes' => 20, 'approver' => $nonStaffId, 'staff' => true, 'reason' => 'ticket', 'accepted' => [true, true, false]],
        ['minutes' => 20, 'approver' => null, 'staff' => true, 'reason' => 'ticket', 'accepted' => [true, true, false]],
        ['minutes' => 20, 'approver' => $approverId, 'staff' => false, 'reason' => 'ticket', 'accepted' => [false, false, false]],
        ['minutes' => 120, 'approver' => null, 'staff' => true, 'reason' => 'ticket', 'accepted' => [true, false, false]],
        ['minutes' => 20, 'approver' => null, 'staff' => true, 'reason' => '', 'accepted' => [false, false, false]],
    ];
    $store = new DatabaseImpersonationGrantStore(connections: app(ConnectionResolverInterface::class), centralConnection: 'pgsql');
    $assertions = 0;

    foreach ($cases as $case) {
        $central->table('root_identities')->where('id', $staffId)->update(['is_staff' => $case['staff']]);
        foreach (ImpersonationProfile::cases() as $index => $profile) {
            $now = now()->toDateTimeImmutable();
            $grantId = (string) Str::uuid();
            $central->table('root_impersonation_grants')->insert([
                'id' => $grantId, 'staff_identity_id' => $staffId, 'account_id' => $accountId,
                'reason' => $case['reason'], 'approved_by' => $case['approver'],
                'created_at' => $now, 'expires_at' => $now->modify('+'.$case['minutes'].' minutes'),
            ]);
            $claimed = $store->claim(new GrantClaim(grantId: $grantId, staffIdentityId: $staffId, accountId: $accountId, profile: $profile, now: $now));
            expect($claimed !== null)->toBe($case['accepted'][$index]);
            expect($central->table('root_impersonation_grants')->where('id', $grantId)->value('used_at') !== null)
                ->toBe($case['accepted'][$index]);
            $assertions++;
        }
    }

    expect($assertions)->toBe(27);
})->group('pg');

{

        $app->bind(

                connections: $app->make(ConnectionResolverInterface::class),

                options: $app->make(TenancyOptions::class),
            ),
        );
        $app->bind(

                connections: $app->make(ConnectionResolverInterface::class),
                cache: $app->make(CacheFactory::class),
                options: $app->make(TenancyOptions::class),
            ),
        );
        $app->bind(
            ResolveTenantFromHost::class,
            static fn (Application $app): ResolveTenantFromHost => new ResolveTenantFromHost(
                manager: $app->make(TenancyManager::class),
                hosts: $app->make(HostAccountResolver::class),
                accounts: $app->make(AccountRead::class),
                container: $app,

        );

                options: $app->make(TenancyOptions::class),

        $app->bind(
            ResolveWorkspace::class,
            static fn (Application $app): ResolveWorkspace => new ResolveWorkspace(
                manager: $app->make(TenancyManager::class),
                resolver: $app->make(WorkspaceResolver::class),
                options: $app->make(TenancyOptions::class),
            ),
        );
    }

    #[Override]
    public function boot(Application $app): void
    {
        $options = $app->make(TenancyOptions::class);
        $router = $app->make(Router::class);

        // Alias only. A route without it keeps the account-wide admin context.
        // Never added to the tenant group: that would force every tenant route
        // through a workspace.
        $router->aliasMiddleware('tenancy.workspace', ResolveWorkspace::class);

        if ($options->hostIdentificationEnabled) {
            // Account is identified before auth: the user row lives in the tenant DB.
            $app->afterResolving(HttpKernel::class, self::prioritiseHostMiddleware(...));

            $router->aliasMiddleware('tenancy.host', ResolveTenantFromHost::class);
            $router->aliasMiddleware('tenancy.status', AccountStatusGate::class);

            // Merge into an existing `tenant` group; do not replace the list. Priority (below)
            // sorts the three entries around StartSession.
            $router->middlewareGroup('tenant', [
                ...($router->getMiddlewareGroups()['tenant'] ?? []),
                ResolveTenantFromHost::class,
                ScopeSessionToTenant::class,
                AccountStatusGate::class,
            ]);
        }

        if (! $options->oidcEnabled) {
            return;
        }

        // loadRoutesFrom skips a cached route file; a naked group does not.
        if (! ($app instanceof CachesRoutes && $app->routesAreCached())) {
            require dirname(__DIR__, 2).'/routes/oidc.php';
        }

        $router->aliasMiddleware('tenancy.oidc.session_lifetime', EnforceSessionLifetime::class);
        $router->middlewareGroup('tenant', [
            ...($router->getMiddlewareGroups()['tenant'] ?? []),
            EnforceSessionLifetime::class,
        ]);

        if (! $options->impersonation->enabled) {
            return;
        }

        $router->aliasMiddleware('tenancy.impersonation.allow', AllowImpersonatedWrites::class);
        $router->middlewareGroup('tenant', [
            ...($router->getMiddlewareGroups()['tenant'] ?? []),
            ImpersonationSessionGuard::class,
            DenyImpersonatedWrites::class,
        ]);
    }

    /**
     * The account is identified before StartSession (so the session handler is built for the
     * account and saved inside it) and before any user resolution; the session is bound to the
     * account right after StartSession and before errors/auth middleware; the status gate follows.
     */
    private static function prioritiseHostMiddleware(HttpKernel $kernel): void
    {
        if (! $kernel instanceof FoundationKernel) {
            return;
        }

        $kernel->addToMiddlewarePriorityBefore(StartSession::class, ResolveTenantFromHost::class);
        $kernel->addToMiddlewarePriorityBefore(
            [ShareErrorsFromSession::class, AuthenticatesRequests::class, AuthenticatesSessions::class],
            ScopeSessionToTenant::class,
        );
        $kernel->addToMiddlewarePriorityAfter(ScopeSessionToTenant::class, AccountStatusGate::class);
    }
}

<?php

declare(strict_types=1);

namespace CoreX\Tenancy\Laravel\Http\Middleware;

use Closure;
use CoreX\Attributes\Spi;
use CoreX\Attributes\SpiKind;
use CoreX\Tenancy\TenancyServiceProvider;
use Illuminate\Http\Request;
use Illuminate\Http\Response;

/**
 * Pure marker — its only job is to be present in a route's middleware list
 * (checked by {@see DenyImpersonatedWrites} via route introspection, not
 * execution order: group-middleware run BEFORE route-middleware, so a
 * "permit" middleware attached to the route could never physically outrun
 * a "deny" middleware from the group). Precedent for an empty middleware
 * used purely as a route-context flag: the package's own `'tenant'` group
 * registration ({@see TenancyServiceProvider}).
 */
#[Spi(kind: SpiKind::Call, since: '1.0')]
final class AllowImpersonatedWrites
{
    /** @return Response|mixed */
    public function handle(Request $request, Closure $next): mixed
    {
        return $next($request);
    }
}

<?php

declare(strict_types=1);

namespace CoreX\Audit\Laravel;

use CoreX\Attributes\Spi;
use CoreX\Attributes\SpiKind;
use CoreX\Audit\Internal\AuditLog;
use Illuminate\Database\Eloquent\Model;

/** @corex-model-extension Exact append-only AuditLog exemption for impersonation write guards; no arbitrary model opt-out. */
#[Spi(kind: SpiKind::Call, since: '1.0')]
final class AuditWriteExemption
{
    public static function permits(Model $model): bool
    {
        return $model::class === AuditLog::class;
    }
}

<?php

declare(strict_types=1);

namespace CoreX\Access\Identity\Laravel;

use CoreX\Access\Access\Laravel\PrincipalIdentity;
use CoreX\Access\Enums\PrincipalType;
use CoreX\Access\Laravel\AuthOptions;
use CoreX\Attributes\Spi;
use CoreX\Attributes\SpiKind;
use CoreX\Context\Contracts\IdentityPasswordRehasher;
use Illuminate\Contracts\Auth\Authenticatable;
use Illuminate\Contracts\Auth\UserProvider;
use Illuminate\Database\Query\Builder;
use Illuminate\Support\Facades\DB;
use Illuminate\Support\Facades\Hash;
use Override;
use SensitiveParameter;

/**
 * The boxed-and-cloud login lane's own {@see UserProvider} (D125, OQ-18
 * variant A): reads a users-shaped table through query-builder, entirely by
 * {@see AuthOptions} identity fields — connection/table/column names — so
 * `axiomasoft/corex-access` never imports a model from `axiomasoft/corex-tenancy` (AC-28). Every
 * lookup goes through {@see query()}, which always applies the "live user"
 * filter (active = true AND deleted_at IS NULL): without it in
 * retrieveById() too, a session survives the very deactivation meant to end
 * it.
 *
 * `retrieveByToken()`/`updateRememberToken()` are permanent no-ops: the
 * frozen `users` DDL (P2.7, D125) carries no `remember_token` column and one
 * is not being added — "remember me" is simply unsupported by this
 * provider.
 */
#[Spi(kind: SpiKind::Call, since: '1.0')]
final class PrincipalUserProvider implements UserProvider
{
    public function __construct(
        private readonly AuthOptions $options,
    ) {}

    #[Override]
    public function retrieveById($identifier): ?Authenticatable
    {
        $row = $this->query()->where($this->idColumn(), $identifier)->first();

        return $this->toPrincipal($row);
    }

    /**
     * No `remember_token` column exists on the configured table (frozen
     * DB_SCHEMA) — remember-me sessions are not supported.
     */
    #[Override]
    public function retrieveByToken($identifier, #[SensitiveParameter] mixed $token): ?Authenticatable
    {
        return null;
    }

    /** No-op — see {@see retrieveByToken()}. */
    #[Override]

<?php

declare(strict_types=1);

namespace CoreX\Tenancy\Laravel\Http\Middleware;

use Carbon\CarbonImmutable;
use Closure;
use CoreX\Attributes\Spi;
use CoreX\Attributes\SpiKind;
use CoreX\Context\Contracts\ImpersonationService;
use CoreX\Tenancy\Laravel\Support\TenancyOptions;
use Illuminate\Http\Request;
use Illuminate\Http\Response;
use Illuminate\Support\Facades\DB;

/**
 * TTL + revocation + banner for an active impersonated session (D144/D147/
 * D149). Registered in the `'tenant'` group AFTER `EnforceSessionLifetime`
 * (same idiom, AC-15) — a session that has outlived either check must die
 * on THIS request, not on a scheduler's next tick. `revoked_at` is read
 * from root on EVERY request without caching (D144): it is the compliance
 * kill-switch, and a cached answer would survive the revocation for the
 * length of the cache TTL.
 */
#[Spi(kind: SpiKind::Call, since: '1.0')]
final class ImpersonationSessionGuard
{
    public function __construct(
        private readonly ImpersonationService $impersonation,
        private readonly TenancyOptions $options,
    ) {}

    /** @return Response|mixed */
    public function handle(Request $request, Closure $next): mixed
    {
        $state = $this->impersonation->state();

        if ($state === null) {
            return $next($request);
        }

        if ($state->expiresAt <= CarbonImmutable::now()) {
            $this->impersonation->stop();

            abort(401);
        }

        $revokedAt = DB::connection($this->options->centralConnection)
            ->table('root_impersonation_grants')
            ->where('id', $state->grantId)
            ->value('revoked_at');

        if ($revokedAt !== null) {
            $this->impersonation->stop();

            abort(401);
        }

        $response = $next($request);
        $response->headers->set('X-CoreX-Impersonation', $state->grantId);

        return $response;
    }
}

availableCommands.name: google-workspace
availableCommands.description: Read this before the first Google Drive, Docs, Sheets or Slides connector call whenever the task creates or changes a Google file. Use this skill whenever the user wants to create or change a Google Doc, Sheet or Slides file in their Google Drive. Triggers include: a request that names Google Docs, Sheets, Slides or Drive and asks to make, edit, format, copy or rename a file; a docs.google.com link with a request to change that file, even a one-line fix or suggested edits; and any follow-up change to a Google file from earlier in the chat, even "change it" or "add a tab". Includes helper scripts for document positions, cell ranges and slide layout. However, if the user asks for a doc, deck or spreadsheet without naming Google, or gives a Google file only as source material for something new, use Claude's own output type instead. Do NOT use for read-only questions about a Google file, or for Word, Excel, PowerPoint or PDF files.

availableCommands.description: Read this before the first Google Drive, Docs, Sheets or Slides connector call whenever the task creates or changes a Google file. Use this skill whenever the user wants to create or change a Google Doc, Sheet or Slides file in their Google Drive. Triggers include: a request that names Google Docs, Sheets, Slides or Drive and asks to make, edit, format, copy or rename a file; a docs.google.com link with a request to change that file, even a one-line fix or suggested edits; and any follow-up change to a Google file from earlier in the chat, even "change it" or "add a tab". Includes helper scripts for document positions, cell ranges and slide layout. However, if the user asks for a doc, deck or spreadsheet without naming Google, or gives a Google file only as source material for something new, use Claude's own output type instead. Do NOT use for read-only questions about a Google file, or for Word, Excel, PowerPoint or PDF files.

1→# axiomasoft/corex-tenancy

Laravel tenancy primitives for CoreX's physical PostgreSQL database-per-account
profile.

## Support impersonation

Enable the OIDC impersonation lane with `corex-tenancy.oidc.impersonation.enabled`.
Choose `corex-tenancy.impersonation.profile`: `standard` (default, 60-minute maximum grant),
10→`regulated` (30 minutes and approval by a different staff identity), or `dev` (480 minutes).
Production `dev` requires `corex.acknowledged_dangerous_modes` to contain
`corex-tenancy.impersonation.profile`. All grants are claimed once atomically and must carry a
reason. `standard` and `regulated` commit correlated central and tenant audit rows before login;
`dev` commits central audit only. Any audit failure denies access and leaves the grant consumed.
The central intent remains if the tenant mirror fails. Hosts may implement
`ImpersonationGrantStore` and `ImpersonationAuditSink`; a custom sink must preserve committed,
fail-closed writes. The current scoped `ImpersonatedModelWriteGuard` instance provides
`allowing()` for a deliberately permitted write.

20→## Optional wakeup root hints

`corex-tenancy.wakeup.driver` defaults to `local_sweep`. With `axiomasoft/corex-wakeup` installed, a cloud
deployment may explicitly select `root_registry`; this enables the advisory `root_wakeup_hints`
table and the `corex:tenancy:wakeup-root-sweep` command. Hints never replace a tenant-local request or
provide authority to select an account connection.

## Package engine and configuration

CoreX owns the account/domain models, physical tenancy engine and synchronous golden-template
30→provisioning. Account identifiers use UUIDv7; account fields are explicit typed columns. The legacy
`root_accounts.data` column is no longer used for model attributes. Existing signup claim and pool
cleanup SQL still use it for idempotency and crash recovery until P08 (D107); retain the column and
these writes until that migration is complete. Saved/deleting model events invalidate the central host cache.

Publish configuration with `php artisan vendor:publish --tag=corex-tenancy-config`. All settings,
including wakeup, use `config/corex-tenancy.php` under `corex-tenancy`. Migrate host overrides from the
previous `tenancy` key; the old key and model/provider configuration knobs have been removed.

## Template integrity
40→

availableCommands.name: google-workspace
availableCommands.description: Read this before the first Google Drive, Docs, Sheets or Slides connector call whenever the task creates or changes a Google file. Use this skill whenever the user wants to create or change a Google Doc, Sheet or Slides file in their Google Drive. Triggers include: a request that names Google Docs, Sheets, Slides or Drive and asks to make, edit, format, copy or rename a file; a docs.google.com link with a request to change that file, even a one-line fix or suggested edits; and any follow-up change to a Google file from earlier in the chat, even "change it" or "add a tab". Includes helper scripts for document positions, cell ranges and slide layout. However, if the user asks for a doc, deck or spreadsheet without naming Google, or gives a Google file only as source material for something new, use Claude's own output type instead. Do NOT use for read-only questions about a Google file, or for Word, Excel, PowerPoint or PDF files.

availableCommands.description: Render the user's morning brief as a styled HTML artifact, or set it up as a recurring weekday task. Use only when the user explicitly asks to run, see, or set up their morning brief, or if they invoke /morning by name. A question about their day, schedule, or calendar is not by itself a request for the brief; answer it directly instead.

availableCommands.name: google-workspace
availableCommands.description: Read this before the first Google Drive, Docs, Sheets or Slides connector call whenever the task creates or changes a Google file. Use this skill whenever the user wants to create or change a Google Doc, Sheet or Slides file in their Google Drive. Triggers include: a request that names Google Docs, Sheets, Slides or Drive and asks to make, edit, format, copy or rename a file; a docs.google.com link with a request to change that file, even a one-line fix or suggested edits; and any follow-up change to a Google file from earlier in the chat, even "change it" or "add a tab". Includes helper scripts for document positions, cell ranges and slide layout. However, if the user asks for a doc, deck or spreadsheet without naming Google, or gives a Google file only as source material for something new, use Claude's own output type instead. Do NOT use for read-only questions about a Google file, or for Word, Excel, PowerPoint or PDF files.

availableCommands.name: user:docs
availableCommands.description: docs (editable docs people share and comment on; the default for any document, named as a doc or not: a document, report, proposal, resume, cover letter, letter, contract, policy, form, template, worksheet, essay, handbook, guide, how-to, cheat sheet, SOP or other writing to keep, share, collaborate on, send, submit, print or sign; a doc exports to Word, PDF, Markdown or Google Docs, so needing a file to send, attach, upload, submit or print is no reason to pick Word, and a file nobody asked for is a doc, not Word; a plan, comparison, summary or notes asked in chat stays in chat; a pasted claude.ai artifact link may be a doc: check with docs tools first; Word or another file format named, tracked changes wanted, or a .docx to change or use as a template → that format's skill): making one → if no docs-connector instructions are in context, call its `guide` (topic.instructions) first; then create the doc (headings only, no body) before any search, file read or plan, even with files attached.

availableCommands.name: execute-plan
availableCommands.description: Execute a PR Plan DAG from a design document. Parses the plan, topologically sorts it, implements PRs in parallel using worktree-isolated subagents, runs mandatory orchestrator-level review, and assembles either a Graphite PR stack or a plain-git branch stack depending on tool availability.

availableCommands.name: implement
availableCommands.description: Run the full implement-review-fix loop using implementer and reviewer personas. Supports effort-based multi-reviewer scaling (2–7 reviewers) with automatic specialization selection. Includes memory-based feedback loop that learns from past review patterns. Loops until all reviewers find 0 issues of any severity.

availableCommands.name: learn
availableCommands.description: Learn from your own Grok Build sessions and tune your setup: add skills for things you keep typing, fix stale skill instructions, and retire skills, plugins, or MCP servers you never use. Use on "/learn", "learn from my traces", "what skills do I never use". Not for summarizing sessions into notes or memory.

availableCommands.name: long-running-background-tasks
availableCommands.description: Required reading before you start, watch, or wait on anything that keeps running after you launch it — background jobs, watchers, scheduled loops, CI, pull requests, training runs, dev servers, long builds. Read it before you launch such work and before you report on its state. Saying where a running job stands counts as working on it. Use when: about to launch, supervise, inspect, diagnose, or report on work that keeps running after it is started.

availableCommands.name: pr-babysit
availableCommands.description: Monitor PRs, fix CI failures, address review comments (human and bot/automated), resolve merge conflicts, and restack stacks. Supports independent PRs, Graphite stacks, and GitHub stacked PRs (gh-stack). Optional ship lands a ready PR bottom-up when every job has passed and no comments remain open.

availableCommands.name: bundled:review
availableCommands.description: Run a reviewer subagent against your whole branch vs main, your uncommitted working state, a named branch, a single GitHub PR, or an entire Graphite/stacked-PR stack (one reviewer subagent per PR). A bare /review defaults to reviewing your uncommitted working state when the tree is dirty, or your whole branch vs main when the tree is clean. Main, local, and branch modes write a review file plus a summary to disk. PR and stack modes post the findings as a PENDING GitHub review for the user to inspect and submit through the UI. Use --main for an explicit clean-tree branch review, --stack for stacked PRs, --submit to publish immediately as COMMENT, or --approve to publish and approve; the default remains PENDING.

content.text:
clearSession выполняет logout до сброса флага имперсонации. getRememberToken возвращает null, поэтому logout не пишет в базу — на этой платформе это не баг.

DatabaseImpersonationService записывает memo и session до успешного login. При перехваченном исключении failStart откатывает изменения.

Если loginUsingId проходит, но последующий шаг в контроллере падает, имперсонация уже активна. Это допустимо.

availableCommands.name: setup-writing-style
availableCommands.description: Learns how the user writes from their own sent messages and docs, and builds a voice profile so future drafts sound like them instead of generic AI. The profile is saved as the my-writing-style skill. Use when the user asks to set up, learn, or capture their writing voice, or complains that drafts sound generic or unlike them and no my-writing-style profile exists. Only for drafting text the user will send as themselves, not for Claude's own replies.

Use only when the user explicitly asks to run, see, or set up their morning brief, or if they invoke /morning by name. A question about their day, schedule, or calendar is not by itself a request for the brief; answer it directly instead.

availableCommands.name: google-workspace
availableCommands.description: Read this before the first Google Drive, Docs, Sheets or Slides connector call whenever the task creates or changes a Google file. Use this skill whenever the user wants to create or change a Google Doc, Sheet or Slides file in their Google Drive. Triggers include: a request that names Google Docs, Sheets, Slides or Drive and asks to make, edit, format, copy or rename a file; a docs.google.com link with a request to change that file, even a one-line fix or suggested edits; and any follow-up change to a Google file from earlier in the chat, even "change it" or "add a tab". Includes helper scripts for document positions, cell ranges and slide layout. However, if the user asks for a doc, deck or spreadsheet without naming Google, or gives a Google file only as source material for something new, use Claude's own output type instead. Do NOT use for read-only questions about a Google file, or for Word, Excel, PowerPoint or PDF files.

availableCommands.name: user:docs
availableCommands.description: docs (editable docs people share and comment on; the default for any document, named as a doc or not: a document, report, proposal, resume, cover letter, letter, contract, policy, form, template, worksheet, essay, handbook, guide, how-to, cheat sheet, SOP or other writing to keep, share, collaborate on, send, submit, print or sign; a doc exports to Word, PDF, Markdown or Google Docs, so needing a file to send, attach, upload, submit or print is no reason to pick Word, and a file nobody asked for is a doc, not Word; a plan, comparison, summary or notes asked in chat stays in chat; a pasted claude.ai artifact link may be a doc: check with docs tools first; Word or another file format named, tracked changes wanted, or a .docx to change or use as a template → that format's skill): making one → if no docs-connector instructions are in context, call its `guide` (topic.instructions) first; then create the doc (headings only, no body) before any search, file read or plan, even with files attached.

content.text:
1→# P07.3 impersonation invariant model

Risk class: auth, transaction, data integrity. PostgreSQL is the supported grant and audit driver.

| Operation | Resource | Invariant and enforcement | Interference path | Evidence |
|:--|:--|:--|:--|:--|
| Claim | Central `root_impersonation_grants` | One `UPDATE ... WHERE` checks unused, unrevoked, unexpired, nonempty reason, staff claimant, profile TTL, and regulated independent staff approver. An ambient central transaction is refused. | Two concurrent claimants serialize on the grant row; only one can update `used_at` from null. | `ImpersonationProfileTest` 27 cells; existing one-use flow test. |
| Start audit | Central `root_account_events` | Commit the event before any tenant mirror or login. Failure denies access; the claim stays used. | Central insert/commit can fail or have uncertain outcome. It is never rolled back by later tenant failure. | `ImpersonationAuditTest` central failure and tenant failure. |
| Tenant mirror | Tenant `sys_audit_log` | Standard and regulated use the stock `SynchronousAuditWriter`, which requires an event snapshot, rejects ambient transactions and commits before returning. Dev omits this mirror. Optional `AuditLogger` and queue settings have no effect. | Tenant insert/commit can fail after central intent commits; login stays closed. | Core writer persistence/transaction tests; tenancy stock writer and failure tests. |
10→| Session/login | Current request session and auth guard | Start records audit before setting impersonation keys and calling login. Login failure clears auth/session before failed audit. Stop clears auth/session before ended audit. | Audit failure cannot leave an opened impersonation session; a failed login leaves a consumed grant. | `ImpersonationTest`, `ImpersonationAuditTest`. |
| Write guard | Scoped guard instance | Only the current instance may temporarily permit an intentional model write; nested calls restore the previous value after exceptions. | Another scoped instance and later requests remain closed. | `ImpersonationWriteGuardTest`. |

No cross-database atomic commit is claimed. Central intent describes the attempted access and can remain without a tenant row after failure (PLAN3.D100). The later schema baseline migration belongs to P08.

availableCommands.name: google-workspace
availableCommands.description: Read this before the first Google Drive, Docs, Sheets or Slides connector call whenever the task creates or changes a Google file. Use this skill whenever the user wants to create or change a Google Doc, Sheet or Slides file in their Google Drive. Triggers include: a request that names Google Docs, Sheets, Slides or Drive and asks to make, edit, format, copy or rename a file; a docs.google.com link with a request to change that file, even a one-line fix or suggested edits; and any follow-up change to a Google file from earlier in the chat, even "change it" or "add a tab". Includes helper scripts for document positions, cell ranges and slide layout. However, if the user asks for a doc, deck or spreadsheet without naming Google, or gives a Google file only as source material for something new, use Claude's own output type instead. Do NOT use for read-only questions about a Google file, or for Word, Excel, PowerPoint or PDF files.

availableCommands.name: user:docs
availableCommands.description: docs (editable docs people share and comment on; the default for any document, named as a doc or not: a document, report, proposal, resume, cover letter, letter, contract, policy, form, template, worksheet, essay, handbook, guide, how-to, cheat sheet, SOP or other writing to keep, share, collaborate on, send, submit, print or sign; a doc exports to Word, PDF, Markdown or Google Docs, so needing a file to send, attach, upload, submit or print is no reason to pick Word, and a file nobody asked for is a doc, not Word; a plan, comparison, summary or notes asked in chat stays in chat; a pasted claude.ai artifact link may be a doc: check with docs tools first; Word or another file format named, tracked changes wanted, or a .docx to change or use as a template → that format's skill): making one → if no docs-connector instructions are in context, call its `guide` (topic.instructions) first; then create the doc (headings only, no body) before any search, file read or plan, even with files attached.

availableCommands.name: google-workspace
availableCommands.description: Read this before the first Google Drive, Docs, Sheets or Slides connector call whenever the task creates or changes a Google file. Use this skill whenever the user wants to create or change a Google Doc, Sheet or Slides file in their Google Drive. Triggers include: a request that names Google Docs, Sheets, Slides or Drive and asks to make, edit, format, copy or rename a file; a docs.google.com link with a request to change that file, even a one-line fix or suggested edits; and any follow-up change to a Google file from earlier in the chat, even "change it" or "add a tab". Includes helper scripts for document positions, cell ranges and slide layout. However, if the user asks for a doc, deck or spreadsheet without naming Google, or gives a Google file only as source material for something new, use Claude's own output type instead. Do NOT use for read-only questions about a Google file, or for Word, Excel, PowerPoint or PDF files.

availableCommands.name: user:docs
availableCommands.description: docs (editable docs people share and comment on; the default for any document, named as a doc or not: a document, report, proposal, resume, cover letter, letter, contract, policy, form, template, worksheet, essay, handbook, guide, how-to, cheat sheet, SOP or other writing to keep, share, collaborate on, send, submit, print or sign; a doc exports to Word, PDF, Markdown or Google Docs, so needing a file to send, attach, upload, submit or print is no reason to pick Word, and a file nobody asked for is a doc, not Word; a plan, comparison, summary or notes asked in chat stays in chat; a pasted claude.ai artifact link may be a doc: check with docs tools first; Word or another file format named, tracked changes wanted, or a .docx to change or use as a template → that format's skill): making one → if no docs-connector instructions are in context, call its `guide` (topic.instructions) first; then create the doc (headings only, no body) before any search, file read or plan, even with files attached.

availableCommands.name: bundled:review
availableCommands.description: Run a reviewer subagent against your whole branch vs main, your uncommitted working state, a named branch, a single GitHub PR, or an entire Graphite/stacked-PR stack (one reviewer subagent per PR). A bare /review defaults to reviewing your uncommitted working state when the tree is dirty, or your whole branch vs main when the tree is clean. Main, local, and branch modes write a review file plus a summary to disk. PR and stack modes post the findings as a PENDING GitHub review for the user to inspect and submit through the UI. Use --main for an explicit clean-tree branch review, --stack for stacked PRs, --submit to publish immediately as COMMENT, or --approve to publish and approve; the default remains PENDING.
